observed_java_model: The metal probe has dpi 100 and Padding 8. Its first state has SVG height 68.0923; de-scaling by 96/100 gives 65.368608, equal to the 11px Verdana title block's 13.368608 text height plus four padding contributions (title top/bottom and empty body top/bottom) plus EntityImageState's fixed 20px outer delta.

The minty probes have dpi 100 and Padding 5. Their state height 55.5923 de-scales to 53.368608, equal to 13.368608 + 4*5 + 20. The 12px unscaled height difference between metal and minty is exactly 4*(8-5).

For the first minty state, width 144.72 and textLength 113.47 de-scale to 138.9312 and 108.9312, a 30px difference equal to two horizontal padding contributions plus the fixed 20px outer delta. The first metal state analog differs by 36px, equal to 2*8 + 20.

The first metal divider is 39.36864 unscaled pixels below the box top and the first minty divider is 33.36864 pixels below it. These are exactly MARGIN 5 + (13.36864 text height + 2*Padding) + MARGIN_LINE 5.

After applying padding only to state title/body blocks, the first minty state matched exactly but every following labeled rank remained 10 unscaled pixels too close and each transition label remained 5 unscaled pixels too far left. That residue is exactly the missing top/bottom and left Display padding on a minty transition label; SvekEdge's separate one-pixel margin was already present.

Across all three probes, inherited and local arrow colors/styles already follow Java. Padding changes the intrinsic state images consumed by Graphviz, so node sizes, coordinates, routes, pseudo-state placement, and the final canvas move while arrow-style ownership remains independently correct.
invariant: For every ordinary state leaf and transition label, Java treats the effective global legacy skinparam Padding as part of each Display text block, not as a cosmetic SVG inset and not as the state style signature's generic Padding property. EntityImageStateCommon creates the title through Display.create8 with the live SkinParam; EntityImageState independently creates the body Display the same way, including an empty body. SvekEdge creates each nonempty link label through Display.create0 with that same SkinParam, then independently wraps the padded block in its one-pixel ordinary or six-pixel self-link margin. Display#getCreole reads SkinParam#getPadding and constructs a SheetBlock1 whose symmetric padding increases both intrinsic width and height and translates its painted glyphs. EntityImageState merges its two already-padded blocks before applying fixed state-image allowances; SvekEdge supplies its padded-and-margined label size to Graphviz. These intrinsic dimensions enter SVEK before routing, so node coordinates, labeled-rank separation, spline geometry, pseudo-state placement, and canvas size must all be consequences of the padded blocks. Theme execution order only selects the effective Padding value: metal supplies 8, minty supplies 5, and a later theme or ordinary skinparam replaces the earlier value. DPI scaling remains a separate final-document transform.
causal_divergence: Rust resolves the themed state font family, size, colors, stroke, rounding, document background, DPI, and arrow channels, but its node and arrow-font models carry no effective global padding. State sizing measures bare title/body glyphs and adds only fixed state-image deltas; transition label sizing measures bare glyphs plus only SvekEdge's independent one-pixel or self-link margin. Final emission likewise omits each Display block's internal translation. Applying padding only to state nodes makes the first state match, but labeled successor ranks remain 2*Padding too close and their text remains Padding too far left, proving the same missing consumer in transition labels. The resulting node and label boxes enter Graphviz undersized, which produces the downstream coordinate and canvas divergence even though arrow color/style ownership is correct.
planned_change: Resolve the last effective ordinary-or-theme global padding record in source order as a finite nonnegative scalar shared by state node and transition-label text-block models. For state nodes, model title and body as separate padded blocks, retain an empty body's padded extent, and shift divider/glyph origins consistently before layout. For transition labels, add 2*padding to the Display block width and height before SvekEdge's existing ordinary/self-link margin, feed that complete label box to Graphviz, and shift emitted glyph origins by padding inside the outer margin. Apply the same dimensions to label composition and painted-bound calculations so link notes and canvas bounds remain coherent. Feed all dimensions to Graphviz before routing and let existing envelope/DPI stages derive coordinates. Do not key behavior to theme names, fixture labels, state count, expected coordinates, or golden dimensions; do not alter arrow precedence or compensate after SVG emission.
